newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan protests to Seoul at construction on island.
newsitem.headline: Japan protests to Seoul at construction on island.

text.p: Japan said on Friday that it had protested to South Korea about continuing construction work on an uninhabited islet claimed by both countries.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Hiroshi Hashimoto said Japan had confirmed that South Korea was still working on a wharf on one of two disputed islets located halfway between the two countries in the Sea of Japan.
The islands, which have a total area of about 23 hectares (about 58 acres), are known as the Tokdos in South Korea and as the Takeshimas in Japan.
Hashimoto said the protest was lodged with the South Korean embassy in Tokyo on Thursday.
The dispute flared in February when South Korea first started the construction work. The issue has inspired anti-Japanese street protests in South Korea.
Both sides have declared a 200-nautical mile economic exclusion zone around their coasts, embracing the islands.

Japan has claimed them since 1905, when it signed an agreement with Korea that led to its colonisation of that country. Korea says its claims to the island date back to the year 512 and are well-documented.

Japan established diplomatic relations with South Korea in 1965, but while economic ties have become close, the relationship is sometimes tense because many Koreans still harbour bitter memories of Japan's 35 years of colonial rule.
Tokyo is also currently locked in a bitter sovereignty dispute with Chinese communities in Hong Kong, China, Taiwan and Macau over a group of islands in the East China Sea.
